The white poodle arrived ten minutes late. Not very late. Just late enough.
She paused outside the café and surveyed the block.
A dachshund relocated from a sunny spot. A terrier abandoned a fire hydrant. A bulldog discovered something fascinating across the street.
She selected a table in the sun. Not because it was empty. Because it was hers.
At least that was the impression. Good bitches create impressions.
She sat for a while. Watching. Not doing much. Which is different from doing nothing.
A few blocks away — or a few thousand miles — a Border Collie was herding sheep. A Chihuahua was running a boardroom.
Two bitches met on a sidewalk. Neither asked the other's name.
Neither cared where the other went to obedience school. Neither asked what the other did for a living.
They exchanged the information that mattered. Then they moved on.
Dogs have been networking this way for thousands of years.
The rest of us are still experimenting.
The bitch was halfway across the park when she changed direction.
The bitch was working. The sheep she was minding were not.
The sheep preferred wandering. The bitch preferred order.
By sunset, the bitch usually won.
Not because she was bigger. Not because she was stronger.
Because she cared more about her job.
The bitch had never met a sheep she couldn't herd.
Some needed encouragement. Some needed guidance.
The bitch left town with the top down. No destination.
And an unreasonable amount of confidence. Some bitches are born to stay.
The bitch escaped three times before lunch. The first time was accidental.
The second was educational. The third was recreational.
By afternoon she had visited two neighbors, investigated a construction site, sampled a hamburger, and made several poor decisions.
She considered the day a success.
The bitch was seriously petite. The chair was bigger than she was.
Nobody seemed to notice. The bitch certainly didn't.
She occupied the head of the table. The others took their seats.
The little bitch was the smallest in the park. This caused her no concern.
A big dog approached. She sniffed him and informed him of the rules.
Another bastard arrived. The bitch clarified some points.
A Shepherd wandered past. The bitch offered guidance.
The bitch stood perfectly still. That made everyone nervous. The Bulldogs shifted their weight. The Pit Bulls watched the exits.
The Labrador reviewed contingency plans. The bitch blinked once. Nobody relaxed.
People often mistake silence for agreement. Patience for weakness.
Stillness for inactivity. The bitch benefits from all three errors.
When louder dogs argued, she listened. When faster dogs rushed, she observed.
After everyone else loudly announced their intentions, she quietly made plans.
The difference mattered. By the time the room realized something was happening, the bitch was finished.
The bitch had three things to do that day. That would have been manageable.
Unfortunately, there turned out to be twelve. And none of them were willing to wait.
The phone was ringing. The coffee was cooling.
Something important had been forgotten. The question was what.
The bitch woke up with a plan. By 9:15 the plan was dead.
A puppy needed attention. A neighbor needed help.
A delivery arrived. A deadline appeared.
Remarkably, things continued working. Not perfectly.
Some bitches enter a room. Other bitches arrive.
Everybody knows the difference. Nobody agrees what causes it.
Most bitches spend part of their lives negotiating status.
A sniff here. A bark there.
A little drama. A little diplomacy.
Then there are the bitches nobody wants to challenge. Not because they're frightening.
The bitch suddenly stopped walking. That was unusual.
The other bitches continued chatting. The Retriever chased a squirrel.
A storm would arrive three hours later. Nobody remembered the storm.
The bitch sensed it first. Something in the air.
Every neighborhood has one. The bitch who knows everything.
The fence is loose. The marriage is shaky.
The line was invisible. It shouldn't be crossed. Everybody knew where it was. Especially the bitch.
Some bitches don't need fences. Or gates. Or warning signs.
They carry a velvet rope with them. The rope moves when they move.
Most of the time nobody notices. Until somebody tries crossing it.
A boundary is not a wall. Walls keep everybody out.
This one stays. That one goes.
This conversation continues. That conversation ends.
The bitch aims to occupy the best seat for every occasion.
Nobody remembered how she got it. Nobody questioned why she kept it.
Bitches enjoy comfort. This is not unusual.
Most dogs enjoy comfort. Humans too.
The bitch elevates it to an art form.
The softest cushion. The warmest patch of sunlight.
The bitch had options. That was not the problem.
The problem was that most were lousy.
Every bitch has barked up the wrong tree. Usually more than once.
The tree looked promising. The tree seemed interesting.
Then a squirrel in the tree started dropping nuts on her head.
Then she noticed worms crawling out of the bark.
The bitch stood on a hill. Below, her little bastards and bitches were making different mistakes.
Did the father of her puppies ask for her paw in marriage?
So they made a litter of bastards and bitches. They are not called litter for nothing.
For him, he didn't care. He threw it away.
She asked for it. Not in so many words.
The bitch had excellent timing. People called it luck.
Everybody loves a lucky bitch. Particularly when she is winning.
The first deal. The first investment.
The first race. The first apartment.
The first bastard. The first divorce.
The lucky bitch shrugs. What else is she supposed to do?
Everything seemed just perfect. Which made everyone nervous.
Everyone but the desperate bitch. For her, the pursuit of perfection was her only hope.
One desperate bitch bought a pool. Another renovated her kitchen.
A third started playing pickleball. A fourth discovered yoga.
The whole neighborhood was supportive. Mostly.
The rich compare themselves to the richer. The beautiful compare themselves to the more beautiful.
The old bitch arrived last. Nobody had been waiting.
Nobody needed to. She always showed.
Young bitches fight for rank. The alpha bitch doesn't need to compete.
She has earned her place on top.
The loudest bitch barks. The alpha bitch listens.
The fastest bitch runs. The alpha bitch walks.
The Collie crossed the finish line. Nobody handed her a crown.
Most bitches imagine their day arriving all at once.
A perfect romance. A standing ovation.
Life rarely cooperates. Most victories arrive disguised as ordinary Tuesdays.
The bitches gathered on the lawn. Some arrived early.
Some arrived fashionably late. One brought snacks. One brought opinions. One brought both. Nobody was surprised.
They had all traveled different roads to reach the same patch of grass.
The alpha bitch. The lap bitch. The lucky bitch. The Underbitch. The witchy bitch. The working bitch. The desperate bitch.
The bitch who barked up the wrong tree.
The bitch who found the right one.
The bitch who stayed. Different stories. Different bitches. Same species.
